questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: Find the HCF of 64 and 96.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: If 25% of a number is 75, find the number.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: A man buys an article for ₹600 and sells it for ₹750. Find his profit percentage.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: Find the simple interest on ₹2000 at 5% per annum for 4 years.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: Find the area of a rectangle with length 15m and breadth 8m.
questions.exp: Area=length×breadth=15×8=120 m².

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: What is the average of the first 10 natural numbers?
questions.exp: Sum of first 10 natural numbers=10×11/2=55. Average=55/10=5.5.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: If a train travels 240km in 4 hours, find its speed.
questions.exp: Speed=Distance/Time=240/4=60 km/h.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.exp: The SI unit of force is the Newton (N), defined as the force needed to accelerate 1kg of mass at 1 m/s².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which law states that an object at rest stays at rest unless acted upon by an external force?
questions.exp: Newton's First Law (Law of Inertia) states that an object remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The acceleration due to gravity on Earth is approximately:
questions.exp: The acceleration due to gravity on Earth's surface is approximately 9.8 m/s².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Sound cannot travel through:
questions.exp: Sound requires a medium to travel and cannot pass through a vacuum, as there are no particles to carry the vibrations.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the chemical formula of common salt?
questions.exp: Common salt (table salt) has the chemical formula NaCl (Sodium Chloride).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which gas is essential for combustion (burning)?
questions.exp: Oxygen is essential for combustion; it reacts with fuel to produce fire and release energy.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The pH of an acidic solution is:
questions.exp: Acidic solutions have a pH value less than 7. Neutral solutions have pH=7, and basic solutions have pH greater than 7.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a noble gas?
questions.exp: Helium is a noble gas, characterized by its stable electron configuration and low reactivity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which organ in the human body is responsible for pumping blood?
questions.exp: The heart is the muscular organ responsible for pumping blood throughout the body via the circulatory system.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Photosynthesis occurs in which part of a plant cell?
questions.exp: Photosynthesis occurs in the chloroplasts of plant cells, where chlorophyll captures sunlight to convert CO2 and water into glucose and oxygen.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which blood group is known as the universal donor?
questions.exp: O- (O negative) blood group is known as the universal donor because it lacks A, B, and Rh antigens, making it compatible with all blood types.

questions.subject: GK
questions.q: Who is known as the 'Father of the Nation' in India?
questions.exp: Mahatma Gandhi is known as the 'Father of the Nation' in India for his leadership in the freedom struggle through non-violent means.

questions.subject: GK
questions.q: India's national bird is:
questions.exp: The Indian Peacock is India's National Bird, known for its vibrant plumage.

questions.subject: GK
questions.q: Which is the highest civilian award in India?
questions.exp: Bharat Ratna is the highest civilian award in India, instituted in 1954.

questions.subject: GK
questions.q: Indian Army Day is celebrated on:
questions.exp: Indian Army Day is celebrated on 15 January every year, commemorating General K.M. Cariappa taking over as the first Indian Commander-in-Chief in 1949.

questions.subject: GK
questions.q: Which is the highest military gallantry award in India?
questions.exp: Param Vir Chakra is India's highest wartime military gallantry award.

questions.subject: GK
questions.q: The Agnipath scheme for Armed Forces recruitment was launched in which year?
questions.exp: The Agnipath scheme was launched by the Government of India in June 2022 for recruitment of Agniveers into the Armed Forces.

questions.subject: GK
questions.q: Which Indian state shares the longest border with Pakistan?
questions.exp: Rajasthan shares the longest border with Pakistan among Indian states, approximately 1,037 km.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: Find the LCM of 18 and 24.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: A shopkeeper gives a discount of 15% on an item marked ₹800. Find the selling price.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: If the perimeter of a square is 48cm, find its area.
questions.exp: Side=48/4=12cm. Area=side²=144 cm².

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: Find the value of: 8² - 5²

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: A can finish a job in 10 days, B in 15 days. How long will they take together?
questions.exp: Combined rate=1/10+1/15=3/30+2/30=5/30=1/6. Together they take 6 days.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: What is 40% of 150?

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with radius 7cm and height 10cm. (π=22/7)
questions.exp: Volume=πr²h=22/7×49×10=1540 cm³.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The unit of work done is:
questions.exp: The SI unit of work done is the Joule (J), equal to a force of one Newton acting over one meter.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which type of lens is used to correct short-sightedness (myopia)?
questions.exp: Concave lenses are used to correct myopia (short-sightedness) as they diverge light rays before they enter the eye.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: What happens to the resistance of a wire when its length is doubled (keeping other factors constant)?
questions.exp: Resistance is directly proportional to length (R=ρL/A). Doubling the length doubles the resistance.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The phenomenon of light bending when passing from one medium to another is called:
questions.exp: Refraction is the bending of light as it passes from one medium to another due to a change in speed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of these elements is a liquid at room temperature?
questions.exp: Mercury (Hg) is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The process of converting a solid directly into gas without passing through the liquid state is called:
questions.exp: Sublimation is the process where a solid changes directly into a gas without becoming a liquid, e.g., dry ice (solid CO2).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the atomic number of Hydrogen?
questions.exp: Hydrogen has atomic number 1, with one proton in its nucleus.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which acid is found in vinegar?
questions.exp: Vinegar contains Acetic acid (CH3COOH), typically 5-8% concentration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which vitamin deficiency causes night blindness?
questions.exp: Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness, as it is essential for the formation of rhodopsin in the eye's rod cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The functional unit of the kidney is called:
questions.exp: The Nephron is the functional and structural unit of the kidney, responsible for filtering blood and forming urine.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which gas do plants absorb from the atmosphere during photosynthesis?
questions.exp: Plants absorb Carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere during photosynthesis to produce glucose and oxygen.

questions.subject: GK
questions.q: Which Indian state is known as the 'Land of Five Rivers'?
questions.exp: Punjab is known as the 'Land of Five Rivers' (Panj-Aab), referring to Sutlej, Beas, Ravi, Chenab, and Jhelum.

questions.subject: GK
questions.q: The Indian Constitution was adopted on which date?
questions.exp: The Indian Constitution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949, and came into effect on 26 January 1950.

questions.subject: GK
questions.q: Which Indian river is known as the 'Ganga of the South'?
questions.exp: The Godavari river is known as the 'Ganga of the South' (Dakshin Ganga), being the longest river in peninsular India.

questions.subject: GK
questions.q: Who composed India's National Anthem 'Jana Gana Mana'?
questions.exp: India's National Anthem, 'Jana Gana Mana', was composed by Rabindranath Tagore.

questions.subject: GK
questions.q: The Param Vir Chakra is awarded for acts of:
questions.exp: Param Vir Chakra is awarded for the most conspicuous acts of bravery or self-sacrifice in the presence of the enemy during wartime.

questions.subject: GK
questions.q: Which is the largest branch of the Indian Armed Forces by personnel strength?
questions.exp: The Indian Army is the largest branch of the Indian Armed Forces by personnel strength, with over a million active soldiers.

questions.subject: GK
questions.q: The 'Siachen Glacier', the world's highest battlefield, is located in:
questions.exp: The Siachen Glacier, often called the world's highest battlefield, is located in the Karakoram range in Ladakh, near the India-Pakistan border.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: Find the value of x: 4x - 7 = 21

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: A sum of money triples itself in 10 years at simple interest. Find the rate of interest.
questions.exp: For sum to triple, SI=2×Principal. Rate=200/Time=200/10=20%.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: Find the circumference of a circle with radius 21cm. (π=22/7)
questions.exp: Circumference=2πr=2×22/7×21=132cm.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: If the ratio of two numbers is 3:4 and their sum is 84, find the larger number.
questions.exp: Total parts=3+4=7. Larger number=(4/7)×84=48.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: Find the square root of 1024.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: What is the compound interest on ₹10000 at 10% per annum for 2 years?

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: A man walks at a speed of 5 km/h. How much time will he take to cover 15km?
questions.exp: Time = Distance/Speed = 15/5 = 3 hours.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which instrument is used to measure atmospheric pressure?
questions.exp: A Barometer is used to measure atmospheric pressure.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The energy possessed by a body due to its motion is called:
questions.exp: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion, given by KE=½mv².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following is a good conductor of electricity?
questions.exp: Copper is an excellent conductor of electricity due to the free movement of electrons in its structure, widely used in electrical wiring.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The frequency of a wave is the number of:
questions.exp: Frequency is defined as the number of oscillations (complete cycles) of a wave per second, measured in Hertz (Hz).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which gas makes up the largest percentage of Earth's atmosphere?
questions.exp: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere, the largest percentage of any gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is used as a bleaching agent?
questions.exp: Chlorine is commonly used as a bleaching agent in textiles, paper, and water purification.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the chemical name for 'quick lime'?
questions.exp: Quick lime is the common name for Calcium oxide (CaO).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Diamond and graphite are both made up of which element?
questions.exp: Both diamond and graphite are allotropes of Carbon, differing only in their crystal structure and bonding arrangement.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which part of the human body produces insulin?
questions.exp: The Pancreas produces insulin, a hormone that regulates blood sugar levels.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: DNA stands for:
questions.exp: DNA stands for Deoxyribonucleic Acid, the molecule that carries genetic information in living organisms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which disease is caused by the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito?
questions.exp: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites transmitted through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito.

questions.subject: GK
questions.q: Who is the current President of India (as of late 2026 standard records)?
questions.exp: Droupadi Murmu has been serving as the 15th President of India since July 2022.

questions.subject: GK
questions.q: Which day is celebrated as 'World Environment Day'?
questions.exp: World Environment Day is celebrated on 5 June every year to promote environmental awareness.

questions.subject: GK
questions.q: The 'Statue of Unity', the world's tallest statue, is located in which Indian state?
questions.exp: The Statue of Unity, depicting Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, is located in Gujarat and stands at 182 meters, the world's tallest statue.

questions.subject: GK
questions.q: India's first nuclear test, 'Smiling Buddha', was conducted in which year?
questions.exp: India's first nuclear test, codenamed 'Smiling Buddha', was conducted in 1974 at Pokhran.

questions.subject: GK
questions.q: Which is the official emblem of the Indian Army?
questions.exp: The Indian Army's official emblem features crossed swords (Khanda style) with the Ashoka symbol, reflecting valor and discipline.

questions.subject: GK
questions.q: The 'Golden Quadrilateral' project connects which four major Indian cities by highways?
questions.exp: The Golden Quadrilateral connects India's four largest metro cities — Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata — via a network of highways.

questions.subject: GK
questions.q: Which branch of the Indian Armed Forces operates the MiG-29 and Tejas fighter aircraft?
questions.exp: The Indian Air Force operates fighter aircraft including the MiG-29 and the indigenously developed Tejas.
